catalog_quote: [p.8, §2.3] A likely explanation for such a distribution of consonants is stress. Mills (1985) states that in Cebara, a related Senufo language, 'Stress is a demarcative, non-distinctive feature serving as a cohesive factor within the word and occurring once in each basic word. It is realized as a long and fortis articulation of the onset consonant of the stressed syllable, and is an intense articulation of the syllable.' (p. 119) She continues by saying that 'stress always occurs on the first syllable of the basic word.' Thus the first consonant of a word is stressed while all other consonants of a basic word are unstressed. [p.15, §3.2.3] Since monosyllabic words inevitably have stress on their only syllable, and since evidence from the behaviour of consonants both in Cebara and Sə̀cə̀té suggests stress on the first syllable and lack of stress on all the remaining syllables of the basic word, the similarity of vowel behaviour on the first vowel of disyllabic words and the vowel of the monosyllabic words can be potentially attributed to stress. [p.16, §3.2.4] The first syllable of a trisyllabic word is stressed. There is a fortis pronunciation of both the vowel and the consonant. [p.18, §4] Each unit has a single tone melody, a single stressed syllable, a single specified vowel, and if there is a medial consonant, it belongs to a very restricted set of consonants ...

new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is demarcative and non-contrastive: it falls on the first syllable of the 'basic word' (phonologically defined unit = a single root plus its suffixes), realised as fortis articulation of the initial consonant and a fully specified first vowel; all following syllables of the unit are unstressed (restricted lenis consonant set /r x ʔ l., vowels copied from the first vowel and centralised/reduced). The language is tonal (three level tones plus contours); stress is independent of tone.
new_statements.secondary_stress: None described as such; phonologically complex words (compounds, root+root nouns such as sa+ka 'goat', and some loans like mara+fa 'gun', ka+laxa 'sorghum') carry one stress per unit, i.e. on the first syllable of each root, diagnosed by a full (non-lenited) consonant and a fully articulated vowel in medial position.
new_statements.exceptions: The noun-class clitic ka is the only morpheme that alternates between stressed (sentence-initial, stop k) and unstressed (after a verbal particle, lenited xa) forms (1987: 17-18). A few words with first vowel [a] and a fully specified second vowel might suggest stress shifted to the second syllable, but Garber rejects this as unsatisfactory because the stressed (fortis) consonant remains word-initial; 'the matter awaits further research' (1991: 17). The 1987 thesis hedges that more research on the segment-stress relation is needed before definite statements (p.38).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonologically defined unit/basic word (root + class/aspect suffixes; in nouns includes the indefinite suffix), not the orthographic or lexical word; compounds = several units, each initial-stressed. Evidence is distributional and impressionistic (consonant inventory by position, lenition, vowel centralisation in phrase-medal position before the question marker la), no instrumental measurements. Garber explicitly models her notion of stress on Mills' description of Cebaara Senufo ('demarcative, non-distinctive.. always occurs on the first syllable of the basic word'). Same analysis already in Garber 1987 ch.1 pp.17-18, 22, 38 ('It was proposed that the first syllable of each word is stressed').
new_statements.identity_note: Garber's data are from Kotoura (Tagba/Sucite area, Comoé-Léraba, SW Burkina Faso); she calls the language Sucite (1987) / Sicite, Sùcìté, Sə̀cə̀té (1988-91) and 'Tagba Senufo' (1998) — all names Glottolog lists under sici1249 itself, so no dialect mismatch. Mori-Traoré 2016 and Traoré 1992 describe the Tagba (səcərə) of Mahon, a neighbouring village of the same language. The stress definition Garber adopts is borrowed from Mills on Cebaara Senufo (ceba1235), but the distributional evidence she gives is Sicite-internal.
